**What kind of error.** On 17:37, word boundaries are the largest single kind but not a majority. Of the 29 edits, 15 are spaces the decoder added where none was sent and 14 are letters (4 wrong, 10 added). Even with spaces costing nothing, 14 edits remain. So in the bench replay the letters are not all right. The plan's "every letter is right, the spaces are wrong" describes what the app printed on the day (the sidecar), not what the test replay reads. Where the key has `WB6RED`, the replay reads `W T E E T E  E ERE D`: single-element letters with spaces between them. That looks like gaps inside characters being read as gaps between words. It is the shape of the fault, not a traced cause; tracing it is step 3's job.

**What was built.**
- **Scorer:** `CwScorer` in the engine test project reports edits, scored length and whether the key is exact or inferred. Its 12 hand-counted test cases failed 12 of 12 against a stub first, then passed 12 of 12.
- **Tie rule:** my first rule for choosing between equally short alignments miscounted one hand case: it split 5 misplaced spaces into a wrong letter, an added letter and 3 spaces. I replaced it before scoring any recording. The new rule leans toward counting spaces, so I print a letters-only count beside it that no tie rule affects. The edit counts don't depend on the rule either way.
- **Tables:** everything is in `docs/phase-correctness/baseline.md`.
